title: Fan builder unveils 183-stud LEGO SHIP with 23,000 pieces
summary: Builder Jean-Philippe Leroux has created a huge custom LEGO spaceship called Northstar for SHIPtember, packing in tens of thousands of pieces and over a hundred LEDs.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Fan builder Jean-Philippe Leroux has completed Northstar, a giant custom LEGO spaceship built for SHIPtember — an annual fan challenge where builders create a 'Seriously Huge Investment in Parts' spaceship measuring at least 100 studs long.

Northstar smashes that minimum, coming in at 183 studs long, weighing roughly 18.3kg (about 40lb), and using an estimated 23,000 LEGO pieces. It's fitted with 102 LEDs, which light up internal cavities built into the design to help save weight and parts while still keeping the model structurally sound.

Leroux says the ship's look was influenced by sci-fi series The Expanse, while its distinctive shaping reportedly came from an unlikely source: a fidget spinner.

This is a fan-made custom creation (MOC), not an official LEGO Group set.

## Why it matters
SHIPtember is a highlight of the fan-building calendar each year, showing off just how ambitious builders can get with scale, lighting and structural engineering using standard LEGO pieces. Builds like Northstar are a great source of inspiration for anyone into large-scale MOCs, display pieces, or pushing techniques like internal lighting and weight management in oversized models.

## What to watch next

title: LEGO's Longest-Ever Set Wasn't Designed to Beat the Titanic
summary: The new UCS Executor Super Star Destroyer has overtaken the Titanic as LEGO's longest set ever, but its designer says that was never the plan.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO's new Ultimate Collector Series set, 75457 Executor Super Star Destroyer, measures a whopping 136cm long — just enough to edge out 10294 Titanic as the longest official LEGO set ever released.

According to designer John Ho, speaking in a roundtable interview with fan media including Brick Fanatics, this record wasn't the design team's goal. Instead, the length came down to part constraints. The engine section was based on an existing model, and the team had limited choices for scaling it — essentially certain Technic wheels or specific brick sizes. Once those fixed points were locked in, the rest of the ship's proportions followed, and the model ended up longer than intended.

In official marketing, LEGO has been careful to describe it as the longest Star Wars model rather than directly claiming the overall longest LEGO set title — even though it does now hold that record.

75457 Executor Super Star Destroyer launches for LEGO Insiders on 1 October, with a wider release on 4 October, priced at £649.99 / €749.99 / $799.99. Buyers who purchase between 1–7 October will get a free 40897 Darth Vader's Lightsaber gift with purchase while stocks last.

## Why it matters
For UCS collectors and display builders, this is a genuinely fascinating look behind the curtain — showing how real engineering and part limitations, not marketing targets, can shape a flagship model's final scale. It's also a useful reminder for anyone planning shelf space: at 136cm, this set needs serious display real estate.

## What to watch next
Expect plenty of comparison photos and reviews once the set officially launches on 4 October, along with discussion over whether LEGO will lean into the "longest set ever" title more directly in future marketing.
